study.title: Regulatory Effects of Acupuncture on Emotional Disorders in Patients With Menstrual Migraine Without Aura: A Resting-State fMRI Study
study.study_design: Randomized clinical trial with two parallel arms; resting-state fMRI pre- and post-treatment
study.randomization: Patients who met the inclusion criteria were randomly assigned to the true acupuncture (TA) and sham acupuncture (SA) groups in a 1:1 ratio
study.blinding: Not fully described; participants in SA group did not experience Deqi; blinding of outcome assessors not explicitly described
study.population: Female patients with menstrual migraine without aura (MMoA), aged 18-50, right-handed, recruited from outpatient clinic of Departments of Neurology and Gynecology
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) female, 18-50 years of age, right-handed; (2) migraine attacks outside of the menstrual cycle did not exceed six per month; (3) a history MMoA for 6 months or more; (4) a stable 28 (±7)-day menstrual cycle; and (5) Zung self-rating anxiety scale (SAS)/Zung self-rating depression scale (SDS) score >50
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) neurological diseases, immunodeficiency, bleeding disorders, or allergies; (2) MRI contraindications, such as claustrophobia; (3) any prophylactic headache medication or any acupuncture treatment during the last 3 months; alcohol or drug abuse; (4) pregnancy, lactation, or plans to become pregnant within 6 months; (5) Zung self-rating anxiety/depression scale score >50; and (6) psychiatric disorders, such as schizoaffective disorder, schizophrenia, organic mental disorder, psychotic features coordinated or uncoordinated with mood or bipolar disorder

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needles are inserted perpendicularly 0.5 to 1 cm (5–10 mm) at non-acupoints using standard stainless steel filiform needles. At 5–10 mm depth, needles reach into muscle/fascia tissue, activating deep mechanoreceptors. This clearly exceeds the superficial (1–5 mm) threshold and qualifies as full penetration (Level 1).

interventions.needle_type_exact: Single-use stainless steel filiform needles (Hwato Needles, Sino-foreign Joint Venture Suzhou Hua Tuo Medical Instruments Co., China)
interventions.needle_size_exact: 25-40 mm in length and 0.25-0.30 mm in diameter
interventions.depth_exact: approximately 0.5-1.5 cm; GB20 punctured obliquely 0.8 to 1.2 cm toward to apex nasi; GB8 punctured horizontally 0.5 to 0.8 cm; PC6 punctured perpendicularly 0.5 to 1 cm; SP6 punctured perpendicularly 0.5 to 1.5 cm; LR3 punctured perpendicularly 0.5 to 1 cm
interventions.manipulation_exact: Needles were twisted and rotated (90° < amplitude < 180°) at a frequency of 1-2 Hz. Stimulation was repeated one to three times to achieve the Deqi sensation
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Yes; Deqi sensation intended (a sensation of soreness, numbness, distention, or radiating that indicates effective needling)
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: 27 or 27 ± 6 sessions according to changes in their menstrual cycle; 9 ± 2 times per menstrual cycle
interventions.treatment_period_exact: 3 menstrual cycles (28 days or 28 ± 7 days per cycle); 12 weeks total
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: Two specialized acupuncturists with at least 5 years of training and 3 years of experience; implemented acupuncture therapy in both groups in turns
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Acupoints selected according to traditional classic and systematic reviews of ancient and modern literature of acupuncture for MMoA upon several consensus meetings with experts based on experiences from previous study
interventions.source_location: Methods: Intervention section, page 4; Table 1, page 3; Table 2, page 4

non_acupoint_locations_exact: At the medial arm on the anterior border of the insertion of the deltoid muscle at the junction of the deltoid and biceps muscles

Halfway between the epicondylus medialis of the humerus and ulnar side of the wrist bilaterally

extraction_notes.note: Baseline attack frequency values appear swapped between Table 3 and Table 4. Table 3 shows TA=3.29±1.59 and SA=3.76±2.35; Table 4 shows TA=3.76±2.35 and SA=3.29±1.59. The between-group p-value is 0.436 in both tables. Values extracted from Table 4 for clinical outcome entries as it is the primary clinical results table.

The exact number of participants analyzed for neuroimaging is not explicitly reported. n_total_analyzed_neuroimaging is left as null. The paper states n=24 TA and n=20 SA for clinical analysis, and these are likely the neuroimaging analysis samples, but the paper does not state this explicitly. Head movement exclusion criteria are stated but final neuroimaging n per group is not specified.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: Participants, Data Analysis sections, pages 3-5

extraction_notes.note: Coordinate space: Tables 5, 6, 7 use column header 'Talairach' for x, y, z coordinates. However, the preprocessing section states images were spatially normalized to 'the standard template' without specifying MNI or Talairach. It is possible these coordinates are MNI-space labeled as Talairach by the DPABI software output. Extraction preserves the reported label 'Talairach' without conversion.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods: Data Analysis, page 4-5; Tables 5, 6, 7, pages 6, 8, 9

extraction_notes.note: No healthy control group was included at baseline (authors acknowledge this as a limitation). Therefore, no baseline case-control contrast for neuroimaging is reported.
No adverse events section is present in the paper. It is unclear whether adverse events were monitored or not.
No blinding success or allocation guessing data are reported. The authors note in limitations that expectancy was not quantified.

Brodmann Area 18 is listed for Superior frontal gyrus (R) at Talairach coordinates 15, -11, 64 in Table 6. BA 18 is occipital (lingual/cuneus), not consistent with superior frontal gyrus. This may be a table error in the paper. The value is extracted as reported.
The cuneus row in Table 6 lists BA as '-' (dash), not a numeric value. Extracted as '-' in brodmann_area_exact.

Correlation r-values for C9 (ACC-SAS) are reported as r=0.49 in text (page 6) and r=0.451, p=0.027 in Figure 5 caption. For C10 (ACC-SDS) r=0.41 in text and r=0.411, p=0.046 in Figure 5 caption. Minor discrepancies between text and figure. Both values noted in the extraction.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Neuroimaging Results page 6; Figure 5 caption, page 9

extraction_notes.note: The baseline correlation result states ALFF in right MTG was 'negatively correlated with VAS (r = 0.29, p < 0.05)' in the text, yet Figure 2 caption states 'ALFF in the MTG was positively correlated with VAS' and the figure shows r = -0.327, p = 0.042. The scatter plot in Figure 2 shows a negative slope, consistent with negative correlation. The r = 0.29 in text appears to refer to the absolute value or is a reporting error. Extracted as reported in text (negative correlation, r = 0.29) but flagged here.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results: Neuroimaging Results page 5-6; Figure 2 caption, page 7

extraction_notes.note: The SA sham acupuncture uses real needles at non-acupoints with penetration to 0.5-1cm depth. No non-penetrating sham device (e.g. Streitberger needle) is used. The sham differs from true acupuncture primarily by location (non-acupoints) and absence of Deqi, not by penetration. This is important for interpreting placebo versus physiological contributions.
